Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zulm 0.0.0.9000

  • First development version: the package skeleton and its family conventions. The R interface follows in later stages.

  • Bundles the CPU subset of ‘ggml’ v0.26.0, built once per instruction-set level (baseline, sse42 and avx2 on x86-64, neon on arm64); the best level the CPU supports is loaded with the package, and options(zulm.variant =) forces another.

  • zulm_info() reports the bundled ‘ggml’ version, the variant loaded, and the CPU features it was built for.

  • Installing from source with ZULM_CFLAGS and ZULM_CXXFLAGS set builds one variant for the local CPU (not on Windows).

  • Parameter stores: zl_params(), zl_param() with init and type ("f32", "f16" or "bf16"), zl_param_get(), zl_param_set(), zl_param_names(), zl_param_count() and zl_param_tensor(); initialisers zl_init_normal(), zl_init_uniform(), zl_init_zeros() and zl_init_ones(), drawing from ‘zurand’ under a key derived from the parameter’s name.

  • zl_save() and zl_load() write and read stores as GGUF files, with metadata, at f32, f16 or bf16.

  • Every error inherits zulm_error and every warning zulm_warning; see ?"zulm-conditions" for the classes. Allocations are checked against getOption("zulm.max_bytes") (4 GiB by default).

  • Graphs: zl_graph() builds a graph once from an R function, zl_int() declares integer inputs, zl_forward() runs it any number of times on new inputs, and zl_graph_info() describes it.

  • Operations on tensors inside a graph: +, -, *, / with broadcasting, zl_scale(), zl_sum(), zl_sum_rows(), zl_mean_rows(), zl_cumsum(), the elementwise functions (zl_sqr() to zl_tanh(), zl_gelu()), zl_swiglu(), zl_crossprod(), zl_reshape(), zl_permute(), zl_t(), zl_cont(), zl_view(), zl_concat(), zl_pad(), zl_get_rows(), zl_where(), zl_clamp(), zl_tri(), zl_softmax() with masks, zl_causal_mask(), zl_rope() in both conventions, zl_rms_norm(), zl_layer_norm(), the losses zl_cross_entropy(), zl_mse() and zl_mae(), and zl_cast().

  • Every argument ‘ggml’ would assert on is checked first; an assertion that still happens while a graph is built is zulm_engine_error.

  • ‘ggml’’s log becomes messages of class zulm_message, at the level of options(zulm.log =) ("warn" by default).

  • Training: zl_adamw() and zl_sgd() describe optimisers; zl_trainer() prepares a graph with a loss for training through ‘ggml-opt’, with gradient accumulation and global-norm clipping (clip_norm); zl_step() trains on one batch, zl_grad() returns a parameter’s gradient, and zl_reset() clears the optimiser’s state. An operation without a gradient between a parameter and the loss is refused with zulm_unsupported_backward, naming it and its call.

  • zl_graph() and zl_trainer() collect garbage when graphs and trainers no longer referenced hold over 128 MB, which R’s collector does not see.

  • The bundled ‘ggml’ carries patches for the gradients of MEAN, SUB and DIV with broadcasting, and for gradient clipping in ‘ggml-opt’.

  • A NaN reaching zl_softmax() no longer stops R, a transposed column enters arithmetic and other kernels correctly, and graphs reserve memory as they grow rather than for the largest graph.

  • Random numbers come from ‘zurand’: zl_seed() sets the session key, zl_rng_uniform() and zl_rng_normal() draw in R, and zl_noise_uniform() and zl_noise_normal() draw inside a graph, anew at each training step. Draws do not depend on the thread count or on how a batch is split.

  • Reported losses (zl_cross_entropy(), zl_mse(), zl_mae(), from zl_step() and zl_forward()) are fixed-order sums of per-row values, so they are the same at any thread count.

Developed by Pedro Baltazar.
